question: Does certify/20c (certify/16e's encoding with its capped size queries solved by deterministic cube-and-conquer over the colours of the first trace prefixes, pruned by distinguishing words) decide more fresh noise-free 20-state worlds than certify/16e at the same conflict budget (B20 2000000, C20 50000), while staying sound, deterministic under a conflict-only stop, faithful, and equal to certify/16e at bound 16?

hypotheses.H1: certify/20c issues no WRONG certificate on 6 fresh 20-state worlds over two passes (12 records) or on 6 eps-0 16-state controls
hypotheses.H2: with a conflict-only stop on a 4-worker pool, the two certify/20c passes give byte-identical canonical records on 6/6 cases with identical conflict counts and 0 hard kills (054 showed this for certify/20t)
hypotheses.H3: every certify/20c record is reproduced exactly by api_checks driving certify/20c observation by observation (run once)
hypotheses.H4: at bound 16 certify/20c gives the same label as certify/16e on 6/6 fresh clean 16-state controls and the same canonical machine for ID (plan 052 IDF-equivalence rule, unchanged). Inferred risk declared pre-data: a satisfying cube may yield a different witness machine than the monolithic call, so canonical M2 may differ; labels may not
hypotheses.H5: certify/20c ID+IDF >= 2/6 on scale20t and strictly more than certify/16e at bound 20 on the same seeds. Inferred risk declared pre-data: in 053 and 054 the least-machine search used most of the budget; splitting may only spread the same hardness over cubes

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify20c.py (certify/20c); certify/16n (FREEZE_050), certify/16e (FREEZE_049), certify/16s (FREEZE_051), certify/20t (FREEZE_054) and every earlier module are imported only, never edited. certify/20c keeps certify/16e's encoding (A16: first-visit symmetry clauses, apartness clauses, observe / propose / result interface, labels, K) and its query sequence (least-machine sizes n_lo upward, then the 'future' and 'start' rival queries at each size up to N). It changes only how each SAT query is solved once its first 50000-conflict chunk is capped: the query is split into cubes and conquered as below. Queries that answer inside the first chunk are solved exactly as in certify/16e.
design.cubes: cube variables are the colours of the states reached by the first d = 5 trace prefixes (positions 0..4 of the trace, in trace order). Under first-visit symmetry these colourings are exactly the restricted-growth strings of length 5 (at most Bell(5) = 52). A cube is pruned before solving if it gives one colour to two prefixes proven apart by a distinguishing word (the apartness relation already in the encoding). Cube order is lexicographic in the restricted-growth string, fixed before solving; no wall time, randomness or solver statistics affect it.
design.conquer: each surviving cube is solved under assumptions on one incremental CaDiCaL instance in round-robin chunks of C20 = 50000 conflicts, in the fixed cube order; a cube returning UNSAT is closed; any SAT cube answers SAT for the query with that witness; UNSAT on every cube answers UNSAT; conflicts across all cubes count against the same case budget B20 = 2000000 (B 3000000 at bound 16 for compat); budget spent -> unknown, exactly as certify/16e's chunked resume
design.soundness: Exact argument, checked by tests and by GS_ref: the cubes partition the colourings allowed by first-visit symmetry of the first 5 prefixes, and pruned cubes are unsatisfiable by the apartness clauses, so SAT/UNSAT of the query equals the disjunction over cubes; labels follow certify/16e's rules unchanged
design.stop: conflict-only stop for all arms; 900 s per-case hard kill as a safety net (any kill fails GDET55)
